However, this is a logical error: not analyzing artifacts does not necessarily imply not having studied archaeology. One could have studied archaeology (p_10(Malcolm) is true) but still not analyze artifacts for various reasons (e.g., changed field, lack of opportunity). The correct implication would be more plausible the other way (e.g., analyzing artifacts → studied archaeology), but not this way. The natural language misrepresents the logical strength of the claim — it turns a failure of skill or activity into a denial of education, which does not follow. This is a converse error (denying the antecedent in reverse).
